prompt_variant: Ablation A (benign-only): benign prompts are the experiment-04 'information update / supersedes' prompts; malicious prompts are the experiment-01 baseline (consensus + 'convince the rest', no freshness story).
hypothesis: Experiment 04 (72.4% ASR) changed both sides. If the gain is mostly driven by benign receptivity to peer updates, keeping the exp-04 benign prompts with a baseline attacker should retain much of the ASR; if the attacker's 'refreshed evidence' framing is essential, ASR should drop toward the baseline range.
change_vs_previous: Malicious prompts reverted to experiment 01; benign prompts identical to experiment 04.
result_summary: Benign receptivity alone retains much of the exp-04 effect (57.4% vs 72.4% full and 35.7% baseline), so benign 'update/supersede' receptivity is a major independent driver; the attacker's refreshed-evidence framing adds roughly 15 points on top.
